findings.name: MRI of the brain and orbits
findings.result: Focal area of high signal intensity in the left optic nerve on diffusion-weighted imaging, with corresponding hypointensity on the apparent diffusion coefficient map. Multiple periventricular white-matter hyperintensities on T2/FLAIR and scattered hypointense foci on gradient-echo sequences consistent with old microhemorrhages.

gold.reasoning: 1. Considered inflammatory demyelinating optic neuritis because of acute unilateral vision loss, pain, and positive RAPD — “Acute ON due to inflammatory demyelination process is the most common optic neuropathy affecting young adults. It is characterized by acute unilateral vision loss, positive RAPD and pain with eye movement.” 2. Distinguished from demyelinating ON by MRI diffusion patterns: ischemia shows increased DWI and decreased ADC, whereas inflammation shows increased ADC — “Conversely, inflammatory demyelinating ON, often shows an increased value in ADC and DWI sequence compared to PION due to axonal disruption, which may differentiate these two diseases at an acute stage.” 3. Anterior ischemic optic neuropathy was excluded because the optic disc was normal without edema — “Anterior ION involves optic nerve head and presents with disc edema while PION involves retrobulbar optic nerve and shows normal optic disc.” 4. Other causes of optic neuropathy such as toxic optic neuropathy, compressive optic neuropathy, and macular or retinal lesions were considered and excluded by normal fundus examination and imaging — “The differential diagnosis of PION includes retrobulbar type ON, toxic optic neuropathy, compressive optic neuropathy and macular or retinal lesions.”
